request.spec:
Anyone using the app first signs in by typing a name; there is no password. The signed-in
name shows on the screen. A sheet is chosen by typing its id and loading it; the active sheet id
shows on the screen, and everything else in the app is kept per sheet. A sheet that has never been
loaded before starts empty. Everything happens on the one screen at /.

agent.result_text:
Sign-in and sheet loading are in, and `bin/e2e` passes (1 test, 1 passed).

**How it works:**
- **Sign in:** you type a name (no password) into `signin-name` and press `signin-submit`. The name then shows in `current-user`. An empty name shows `signin-error`.
- **Loading a sheet:** you type an id into `sheet-id-input` and press `sheet-load`. This calls `POST /api/sheets/{id}/load`, which sends the user's name in an `X-User` header. If the sheet doesn't exist yet, the server creates it empty. Loading the same id again just reads it back from the store.
- **Display:** once a sheet loads, its id shows in `sheet-current-id`. An empty id or a failed load shows `sheet-error`, which clears when you edit the field or try again.

**What I added:**
- **Stored data:** a Flyway migration (`V1__sheet.sql`) creating a `sheet` table with the id and who created it.
- **Server:** the usual Spring classes in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/sheet/` (entity, repository, service, controller). If two users load the same new id at the same moment, the second one gets the sheet the first created rather than an error.
- **Front end:** a `Session` service (`core/session.ts`) holding the signed-in user and active sheet as signals, and the one screen in `features/home/home.ts`.

The signed-in name lives only in the page's memory, so reloading the browser signs you out. The spec writes no audit records, so I didn't add any.
